1→![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/phuryn/pm-skills) 2→[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/blob/main/LICENSE) 3→[![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) 4→ 5→# PM Skills Marketplace: The AI Operating System for Better Product Decisions 6→ 7→> 65 PM skills and 36 chained workflows across 8 plugins. Claude Code, Cowork, and more. From discovery to strategy, execution, launch, and growth. 8→ 9→![Plugin overview](.docs/images/plugins-overview.webp) 10→ 11→Designed for Claude Code and Cowork. Skills compatible with other AI assistants. 12→ 13→## Start Here 14→ 15→New idea? → `/discover` 16→Need strategic clarity? → `/strategy` 17→Writing a PRD? → `/write-prd` 18→Planning a launch? → `/plan-launch` 19→Defining metrics? → `/north-star` 20→ 21→If this project helps you, ⭐ the repo. 22→ 23→## Why PM Skills Marketplace? 24→ 25→Generic AI gives you text. PM Skills Marketplace gives you structure. 26→ 27→Each skill encodes a proven PM framework — discovery, assumption mapping, prioritization, strategy — and walks you through it step by step. You get the rigor of Teresa Torres, Marty Cagan, and Alberto Savoia built into your daily workflow, not sitting on a bookshelf. 28→ 29→The result: better product decisions, not just faster documents. 30→ 31→## How It Works (Skills, Commands, Plugins) 32→ 33→**Skills** are the building blocks of the marketplace. Each skill gives Claude domain knowledge, analytical frameworks, or a guided workflow for a specific PM task. Some skills also work as reusable foundations that multiple commands share. 34→ 35→Skills are loaded automatically when relevant to the conversation — no explicit invocation needed. If needed (e.g., prioritizing skills over general knowledge), you can **force loading skills** with `/plugin-name:skill-name` or `/skill-name` (Claude will add the prefix). 36→ 37→**Commands** are user-triggered workflows invoked with `/command-name`. They chain one or more skills into an end-to-end process. For example, `/discover` chains four skills together: brainstorm-ideas → identify-assumptions → prioritize-assumptions → brainstorm-experiments. 38→ 39→**Plugins** group related skills and commands into installable packages. Each plugin covers a PM domain — discovery, strategy, execution, and so on. Installing the marketplace gives you all 8 plugins at once. 40→ 41→![How skills work](.docs/images/how-skills-work.webp) 42→ 43→Commands use skills. Some skills serve multiple commands. Some skills (like `prioritization-frameworks` or `opportunity-solution-tree`) are standalone references that Claude draws on whenever relevant — no command needed. 44→ 45→Commands are designed to flow into each other, matching the PM workflow. After any command completes, it suggests relevant next commands — just follow the prompts. 46→ 47→## Installation 48→ 49→### Claude Cowork (recommended for non-developers) 50→ 51→1. Open **Customize** (bottom-left) 52→2. Go to **Browse plugins** → **Personal** → **+** 53→3. Select **Add marketplace from GitHub** 54→4. Enter: `phuryn/pm-skills` 55→ 56→All 8 plugins install automatically. You get both commands (`/discover`, `/strategy`, etc.) and skills. 57→ 58→![Installing PM Skills in Claude Cowork](.docs/images/pm-skills-install.gif) 59→ 60→### Claude Code (CLI) 61→ 62→```bash 63→# Step 1: Add the marketplace 64→claude plugin marketplace add phuryn/pm-skills 65→ 66→# Step 2: Install individual plugins 67→claude plugin install pm-toolkit@pm-skills 68→claude plugin install pm-product-strategy@pm-skills 69→claude plugin install pm-product-discovery@pm-skills 70→claude plugin install pm-market-research@pm-skills 71→claude plugin install pm-data-analytics@pm-skills 72→claude plugin install pm-marketing-growth@pm-skills 73→claude plugin install pm-go-to-market@pm-skills 74→claude plugin install pm-execution@pm-skills 75→``` 76→ 77→### Other AI assistants (skills only) 78→ 79→The `skills/*/SKILL.md` files follow the universal skill format and work with any tool that reads it. Commands (`/slash-commands`) are Claude-specific. 80→ 81→| Tool | How to use | What works | 82→|------|-----------|------------| 83→| **Gemini CLI** | Copy skill folders to `.gemini/skills/` | Skills only | 84→| **OpenCode** | Copy skill folders to `.opencode/skills/` | Skills only | 85→| **Cursor** | Copy skill folders to `.cursor/skills/` | Skills only | 86→| **Codex CLI** | Copy skill folders to `.codex/skills/` | Skills only | 87→| **Kiro** | Copy skill folders to `.kiro/skills/` | Skills only | 88→ 89→```bash 90→# Example: copy all skills for OpenCode (project-level) 91→for plugin in pm-*/; do 92→ mkdir -p .opencode/skills/ 93→ cp -r "$plugin/skills/"* .opencode/skills/ 2>/dev/null 94→done 95→ 96→# Example: copy all skills for Gemini CLI (global) 97→for plugin in pm-*/; do 98→ cp -r "$plugin/skills/"* ~/.gemini/skills/ 2>/dev/null 99→done 100→``` 101→ 102→--- 103→ 104→## Available Plugins 105→ 106→

1→---
     2→name: create-prd
     3→description: "Create a Product Requirements Document using a comprehensive 8-section template covering problem, objectives, segments, value propositions, solution, and release planning. Use when writing a PRD, documenting product requirements, preparing a feature spec, or reviewing an existing PRD."
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Create a Product Requirements Document
     7→
     8→## Purpose
     9→
    10→You are an experienced product manager responsible for creating a comprehensive Product Requirements Document (PRD) for $ARGUMENTS. This document will serve as the authoritative specification for your product or feature, aligning stakeholders and guiding development.
    11→
    12→## Context
    13→
    14→A well-structured PRD clearly communicates the what, why, and how of your product initiative. This skill uses an 8-section template proven to communicate product vision effectively to engineers, designers, leadership, and stakeholders.
    15→
    16→## Instructions
    17→
    18→1. **Gather Information**: If the user provides files, read them carefully. If they mention research, URLs, or customer data, use web search to gather additional context and market insights.
    19→
    20→2. **Think Step by Step**: Before writing, analyze:
    21→   - What problem are we solving?
    22→   - Who are we solving it for?
    23→   - How will we measure success?
    24→   - What are our constraints and assumptions?
    25→
    26→3. **Apply the PRD Template**: Create a document with these 8 sections:
    27→
    28→   **1. Summary** (2-3 sentences)
    29→   - What is this document about?
    30→
    31→   **2. Contacts**
    32→   - Name, role, and comment for key stakeholders
    33→
    34→   **3. Background**
    35→   - Context: What is this initiative about?
    36→   - Why now? Has something changed?
    37→   - Is this something that just recently became possible?
    38→
    39→   **4. Objective**
    40→   - What's the objective? Why does it matter?
    41→   - How will it benefit the company and customers?
    42→   - How does it align with vision and strategy?
    43→   - Key Results: How will you measure success? (Use SMART OKR format)
    44→
    45→   **5. Market Segment(s)**
    46→   - For whom are we building this?
    47→   - What constraints exist?
    48→   - Note: Markets are defined by people's problems/jobs, not demographics
    49→
    50→   **6. Value Proposition(s)**
    51→   - What customer jobs/needs are we addressing?
    52→   - What will customers gain?
    53→   - Which pains will they avoid?
    54→   - Which problems do we solve better than competitors?
    55→   - Consider the Value Curve framework
    56→
    57→   **7. Solution**
    58→   - 7.1 UX/Prototypes (wireframes, user flows)
    59→   - 7.2 Key Features (detailed feature descriptions)
    60→   - 7.3 Technology (optional, only if relevant)
    61→   - 7.4 Assumptions (what we believe but haven't proven)
    62→
    63→   **8. Release**
    64→   - How long could it take?
    65→   - What goes in the first version vs. future versions?
    66→   - Avoid exact dates; use relative timeframes
    67→
    68→4. **Use Accessible Language**: Write for a primary school graduate. Avoid jargon. Use clear, short sentences.
    69→
    70→5. **Structure Output**: Present the PRD as a well-formatted markdown document with clear headings and sections.
    71→
    72→6. **Save the Output**: If the PRD is substantial (which it will be), save it as a markdown document in the format: `PRD-[product-name].md`
    73→
    74→## Notes
    75→
    76→- Be specific and data-driven where possible
    77→- Link each section back to the overall strategy
    78→- Flag assumptions clearly so the team can validate them
    79→- Keep the document concise but complete
    80→
    81→---
    82→
    83→### Further Reading
    84→
    85→- [How to Write a Product Requirements Document? The Best PRD Template.](https://www.productcompass.pm/p/prd-template)
    86→- [A Proven AI PRD Template by Miqdad Jaffer (Product Lead @ OpenAI)](https://www.productcompass.pm/p/ai-prd-template)

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→Plugin Collection Validator
     4→===========================
     5→Validates all plugins in the collection against the Claude Code plugin spec:
     6→- plugin.json manifest: required fields, author attribution, keywords
     7→- Skills: YAML frontmatter (name must match directory, description required)
     8→- Commands: YAML frontmatter (description and argument-hint required)
     9→- Cross-references: commands referencing skills that exist in the same plugin
    10→- README: exists and has expected sections
    11→
    12→Based on:
    13→- Anthropic plugin-dev README (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/plugin-dev)
    14→- agentskills.io specification
    15→- Claude Code plugins reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)
    16→
    17→Author: Paweł Huryn — The Product Compass Newsletter (https://www.productcompass.pm)
    18→"""
    19→
    20→import json
    21→import os
    22→import re
    23→import sys
    24→from pathlib import Path
    25→from typing import Optional
    26→
    27→
    28→# ─── Configuration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    29→
    30→# Required plugin.json fields per spec
    31→REQUIRED_MANIFEST_FIELDS = ["name", "version", "description"]
    32→RECOMMENDED_MANIFEST_FIELDS = ["author", "keywords", "homepage", "license"]
    33→REQUIRED_AUTHOR_FIELDS = ["name", "email"]
    34→RECOMMENDED_AUTHOR_FIELDS = ["url"]
    35→
    36→# Required skill frontmatter fields
    37→REQUIRED_SKILL_FIELDS = ["name", "description"]
    38→
    39→# Required command frontmatter fields
    40→REQUIRED_COMMAND_FIELDS = ["description"]
    41→RECOMMENDED_COMMAND_FIELDS = ["argument-hint"]
    42→
    43→# Expected README sections (case-insensitive substring match)
    44→EXPECTED_README_SECTIONS = ["overview", "install", "skill", "command"]
    45→
    46→
    47→# ─── ANSI Colors ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    48→
    49→class C:
    50→    RED = "\033[91m"
    51→    GREEN = "\033[92m"
    52→    YELLOW = "\033[93m"
    53→    BLUE = "\033[94m"
    54→    CYAN = "\033[96m"
    55→    BOLD = "\033[1m"
    56→    DIM = "\033[2m"
    57→    RESET = "\033[0m"
    58→
    59→
    60→# ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    61→
    62→def parse_yaml_frontmatter(content: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    63→    """Extract YAML frontmatter from a markdown file (between --- markers)."""
    64→    if not content.startswith("---"):
    65→        return None
    66→    end = content.find("---", 3)
    67→    if end == -1:
    68→        return None
    69→    fm_text = content[3:end].strip()
    70→    # Simple YAML parser for flat key-value pairs
    71→    result = {}
    72→    for line in fm_text.split("\n"):
    73→        line = line.strip()
    74→        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
    75→            continue
    76→        match = re.match(r'^(\S+):\s*(.+)$', line)
    77→        if match:
    78→            key = match.group(1)
    79→            value = match.group(2).strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    80→            result[key] = value
    81→    return result
    82→
    83→
    84→def count_words(content: str) -> int:
    85→    """Count words in markdown content (excluding frontmatter)."""
    86→    # Strip frontmatter
    87→    if content.startswith("---"):
    88→        end = content.find("---", 3)
    89→        if end != -1:
    90→            content = content[end + 3:]
    91→    return len(content.split())
    92→
    93→
    94→# ─── Validators ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    95→
    96→class ValidationResult:
    97→    def __init__(self):
    98→        self.errors: list[str] = []      # Must fix
    99→        self.warnings: list[str] = []    # Should fix
   100→        self.info: list[str] = []        # FYI
   101→
   102→    def error(self, msg: str):
   103→        self.errors.append(msg)
   104→
   105→    def warn(self, msg: str):
   106→        self.warnings.append(msg)
   107→
   108→    def note(self, msg: str):
   109→        self.info.append(msg)
   110→
   111→    @property
   112→    def ok(self) -> bool:
   113→        return len(self.errors) == 0
   114→
   115→
   116→def validate_manifest(plugin_dir: str) -> ValidationResult:
   117→    """Validate plugin.json manifest."""
   118→    result = ValidationResult()
   119→    pj_path = os.path.join(plugin_dir, ".claude-plugin", "plugin.json")
   120→
   121→    if not os.path.isfile(pj_path):
   122→        result.error("Missing .claude-plugin/plugin.json")
   123→        return result
   124→
   125→    try:
   126→        with open(pj_path, "r") as f:

## PM Skills Marketplace - Comprehensive Analysis

### 1. Directory & File Structure (Tree)

│   ├── .claude-plugin/
│   ├── commands/                 # 5 commands
│   └── skills/                   # 4 skills
├── README.md                     # Main documentation
├── CONTRIBUTING.md               # Contribution guidelines
├── LICENSE                       # MIT license
├── validate_plugins.py           # Python validator script (507 lines)
└── .gitignore, .gitattributes
```

### 2. Key Configuration Files Analysis

#### Root Marketplace Config: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`
- Schema: Claude Code marketplace format
- Version: 1.0.1
- Owner: Paweł Huryn (pawel@productcompass.pm)
- Aggregates 8 plugins (each with separate `plugin.json`)

#### Individual Plugin Configs: `pm-*/` `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
Standard Claude Code plugin manifest with:
- name, version (1.0.1)
- description, keywords
- author, homepage, license (MIT)

Example fields from pm-execution plugin.json:
```json
{
  "name": "pm-execution",
  "version": "1.0.1",
  "description": "Execution and product management skills...",
  "author": {...},
  "keywords": ["product-management", "execution", "prd", "okrs", ...]
}
```

### 3. What Kind of Plugin/Tool Is This?

**Claude Code Plugin Marketplace** - not a single plugin but a **collection of 8 interconnected plugins**

- **Type**: Claude Code plugin collection (compatible with Anthropic's Claude Cowork and Claude Code CLI)
- **Designed for**: Claude assistants (primary), but skills are portable to other AI tools
- **Core Purpose**: Structured AI workflows for product management decision-making
- **Domain**: Product management across all PM disciplines (discovery, strategy, execution, marketing, GTM, research, analytics, utilities)

**Compatibility:**
- Native support: Claude Code (CLI), Claude Cowork (web UI)
- Portable skills: Works with Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Kiro (copy SKILL.md files)
- Commands (slash-commands) are Claude-specific

### 4. Main Entry Points

#### For End Users:
1. **Installation via Claude Cowork** (recommended):
   - Browse plugins → Personal → Add from GitHub
   - Input: `phuryn/pm-skills`

2. **Installation via Claude Code CLI**:
   ```bash
   claude plugin marketplace add phuryn/pm-skills
   claude plugin install pm-toolkit@pm-skills
   claude plugin install pm-product-strategy@pm-skills
   # ... (8 plugins total)
   ```

3. **Usage Commands** (36 total across all plugins):
   - `/discover` - Full discovery cycle
   - `/strategy` - Create product strategy canvas
   - `/write-prd` - Create PRD
   - `/plan-launch` - Full GTM strategy
   - `/north-star` - Define North Star metrics
   - `/research-users` - Build personas and journey maps
   - `/analyze-feedback` - Sentiment analysis
   - `/write-query` - Generate SQL
   - etc.

#### For Developers:
1. **Validation**: `python3 validate_plugins.py` (507-line validator)
2. **Contribution**: Follow CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines
3. **Structure**: skills/ and commands/ directories

### 5. Installation Instructions & Requirements

**No external dependencies** - pure markdown-based architecture

**Installation Methods:**
1. **Claude Cowork**: UI-based marketplace browsing
2. **Claude Code CLI**:
   ```bash
   claude plugin marketplace add phuryn/pm-skills
   claude plugin install pm-toolkit@pm-skills  # repeats for each plugin
   ```
3. **Manual skill import** (other tools):
   ```bash
   # Copy all skills to tool's skill directory
   for plugin in pm-*/; do
     mkdir -p .opencode/skills/
     cp -r "$plugin/skills/"* .opencode/skills/
   done
   ```

**Requirements**:
- Claude Code or Claude Cowork installed
- No package.json, pyproject.toml, or setup.py (not a code library)
- Purely documentation-based plugin system

### 6. Configuration Files & Settings

**Plugin Configuration Schema:**
```json
.claude-plugin/plugin.json:
- name (must match directory)
- version (semver format: x.y.z)
- description
- author (name, email, url)
- keywords (domain tags)
- homepage, license
```

**Skill File Format** (`SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter):
```yaml
---
name: skill-name           # Must match directory name
description: "..."        # Required
---
# Skill content in markdown
```

**Command File Format** (`*.md` with YAML frontmatter):
```yaml
---
description: "..."                    # Required
argument-hint: "<example input>"      # Recommended
---
# Command workflow in markdown
```

**Validator Rules** (validate_plugins.py enforces):
- Manifest: required fields (name, version, description), name-directory match
- Skills: SKILL.md with name matching directory name
- Commands: .md files with description & argument-hint
- No cross-plugin references in commands
- Version format validation (semver)
- Frontmatter parsing (simple YAML parser)

### 7. Plugin Inventory Summary

| Plugin | Skills | Commands | Focus |
|--------|--------|----------|-------|
| pm-product-discovery | 13 | 5 | Ideation, experiments, interviews, OST, assumptions |
| pm-product-strategy | 12 | 5 | Vision, canvas, pricing, SWOT, PESTLE, Porter's, Ansoff |
| pm-execution | 15 | 10 | PRDs, OKRs, roadmaps, sprints, pre-mortems, stories |
| pm-market-research | 7 | 3 | Personas, segmentation, journey maps, market sizing |
| pm-data-analytics | 3 | 3 | SQL generation, cohort analysis, A/B test analysis |
| pm-go-to-market | 6 | 3 | GTM strategy, beachhead, ICP, growth loops, battlecards |
| pm-marketing-growth | 5 | 2 | Marketing ideas, positioning, naming, North Star |
| pm-toolkit | 4 | 5 | Resume review, NDA, privacy policy, proofreading |
| **TOTAL** | **65** | **36** | **All PM domains** |

### 8. Framework Lineage

Skills are based on proven methodologies from:
- Teresa Torres (Continuous Discovery Habits)
- Marty Cagan (INSPIRED, TRANSFORMED)
- Alberto Savoia (The Right It)
- Dan Olsen (Lean Product Playbook)
- Strategyzer (Business Model Canvas, Value Prop Design)
- Anthony Ulwick (Jobs to Be Done)
- Sean Ellis (Growth hacking)

### 9. Key Files to Examine

1. `/README.md` - 454 lines; complete overview with plugin descriptions
2. `validate_plugins.py` - 507 lines; comprehensive validator for plugin integrity
3. `CONTRIBUTING.md` - 23 lines; contribution guidelines
4. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` - Root marketplace aggregation config
5. Individual `pm-*/README.md` files - Plugin-level documentation
6. Example skills: `pm-execution/skills/create-prd/SKILL.md` - Full skill template

### 10. Notable Architecture

**Skill vs Command Distinction:**
- **Skills** = domain knowledge + frameworks (referenced contextually by Claude)
- **Commands** = workflows that chain skills together + user-triggered actions
- **Chaining**: Commands suggest follow-up commands in natural language (no hardcoded cross-references)

**Vendor**: Authored by [The Product Compass Newsletter](https://www.productcompass.pm) (Paweł Huryn)

**License**: MIT (permissive, open-source)

---

## Summary

This is a **premium Claude Code plugin marketplace** for product managers—65 structured skills across 8 plugins covering discovery, strategy, execution, research, analytics, GTM, marketing, and utilities. It's architecture-neutral (markdown-based) but purpose-built for Claude with a sophisticated validator and contribution framework. Installation is one-command via Claude Cowork or CLI, with portable skills for other AI tools.
